title: 281. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Absolute Value Function Vertex and Shape
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Vertex of the Basic Absolute Value Function
questions.learningObjective: Identify the vertex of the graph of \(y=|x|\).
questions.question: The graph of \(y=|x|\) has its vertex at which point?
questions.explanation: For \(y=|x|\), the minimum value occurs when the expression inside the absolute value is zero. Set \(x=0\), then \(y=|0|=0\). Therefore, the vertex is \((0,0)\). The point \((1,1)\) lies on the graph but is not the vertex.
questions.hint: The vertex of \(y=|x|\) occurs where the expression inside the absolute value equals zero.

questions.concept: Vertex of a Translated Absolute Value Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the vertex of a function written in the form \(y=|x-h|+k\).
questions.question: What is the vertex of the graph of \(y=|x-3|+2\)?
questions.explanation: For \(y=|x-3|+2\), the expression inside the absolute value is \(x-3\). Set \(x-3=0\), so \(x=3\). Then \(y=|3-3|+2=2\). Therefore, the vertex is \((3,2)\). The option \((-3,2)\) comes from reversing the sign of the horizontal shift.
questions.hint: Rewrite the expression as \(x-3=x-(3)\) to identify the horizontal shift.

questions.concept: Direction of Opening of an Absolute Value Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether an absolute value graph opens upward or downward from its equation.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=-|x|\) opens in which direction?
questions.explanation: The graph of \(y=|x|\) opens upward. The negative sign in \(y=-|x|\) reflects the graph across the \(x\)-axis. Therefore, the graph opens downward.
questions.hint: The sign of the coefficient multiplying \(|x|\) determines the vertical direction of the V-shape.

questions.concept: Vertex of a Horizontally Shifted Absolute Value Function
questions.question: What is the vertex of the graph of \(y=|x+4|-1\)?
questions.explanation: Set the expression inside the absolute value equal to zero: \(x+4=0\), so \(x=-4\). Then \(y=|-4+4|-1=-1\). Therefore, the vertex is \((-4,-1)\). The option \((4,-1)\) incorrectly treats the shift as \({+4}\) rather than \(-4\).
questions.hint: Write \(x+4\) as \(x-(-4)\) to read the horizontal shift correctly.

questions.concept: Axis of Symmetry of an Absolute Value Function
questions.learningObjective: Identify the axis of symmetry from the vertex form of an absolute value function.
questions.question: What is the axis of symmetry of the graph of \(y=|x-2|+5\)?
questions.explanation: The vertex of \(y=|x-2|+5\) occurs when \(x-2=0\), so \(x=2\). The vertex is \((2,5)\). The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through the vertex, so it is \(x=2\).
questions.hint: The axis of symmetry is a vertical line passing through the vertex.

questions.concept: Effect of the Leading Coefficient on the Shape of an Absolute Value Graph
questions.learningObjective: Compare the width of \(y=3|x|\) with that of \(y=|x|\).
questions.question: Compared with the graph of \(y=|x|\), the graph of \(y=3|x|\) is:
questions.explanation: For \(y=a|x|\), if \(a>1\), the V-shape is vertically stretched. This makes the graph steeper and narrower than \(y=|x|\). Since \(3>1\), the graph of \(y=3|x|\) is narrower.

questions.concept: Vertex of a Shifted Absolute Value Function
questions.question: What is the vertex of the graph of \(y=|x+1|-3\)?
questions.explanation: Set the expression inside the absolute value equal to zero: \(x+1=0\), so \(x=-1\). Then \(y=|-1+1|-3=-3\). Therefore, the vertex is \((-1,-3)\). The option \((1,-3)\) reverses the horizontal shift.
questions.hint: Find the \(x\)-value that makes the expression inside the absolute value zero.

questions.concept: Range of an Absolute Value Function
questions.question: What is the range of the function \(y=|x-2|+4\)?
questions.explanation:
For all real \(x\), \(|x-2|\ge 0\). Therefore,
\[
y=|x-2|+4\ge 0+4=4
\]
The minimum value is \(4\), attained when \(x=2\). Thus the range is \(y\ge 4\).
questions.hint: Start from the fact that an absolute value is always nonnegative.

questions.concept: Constructing an Absolute Value Function from Its Vertex and a Point
questions.learningObjective: Determine the equation of an absolute value function given its vertex and one additional point.
questions.question: An absolute value function has vertex \((2,-3)\), opens upward, and passes through \((0,-1)\). Which equation represents it?
questions.explanation:
Use the vertex form \(y=a|x-h|+k\). With vertex \((2,-3)\), this becomes
\[
y=a|x-2|-3
\]
Substitute \((0,-1)\), then solve for \(a\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
-1 &= a|0-2|-3\\
&= 2a-3\\
2a &= 2\\
a &= 1
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, \(y=|x-2|-3\).
Option B gives \(y=1\) at \(x=0\), not \(-1\), so it is incorrect.
questions.hint: Substitute the vertex into \(y=a|x-h|+k\), then use the given point to find \(a\).

questions.concept: Constructing a Downward-Opening Absolute Value Function from Graph Data
questions.learningObjective: Determine the equation of a downward-opening absolute value function from its vertex and a point.
questions.question: An absolute value function has vertex \((-2,3)\), opens downward, and passes through \((-4,1)\). Which equation represents it?
questions.explanation:
Using vertex form, \(y=a|x-h|+k\), with vertex \((-2,3)\), we get
\[
y=a|x+2|+3
\]
Since the graph opens downward, \(a<0\). Substitute \((-4,1)\), then solve for \(a\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
1 &= a|-4+2|+3\\
&= a(2)+3\\
&= 2a+3\\
2a &= -2\\
a &= -1
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore, \(y=-|x+2|+3\).
Option A opens upward and gives \(y=5\) at \(x=-4\), so it is incorrect.
questions.hint: Use the vertex form \(y=a|x-h|+k\); the downward opening tells you the sign of \(a\).
